title: Long-term Improvement of Functional and Emotional Quality of Life through ERAS: Risk Factors of PICS and CPSP in Cardiac Surgery
summary: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols are designed to help patients recover more quickly after surgery. Pain therapy plays a central role here, as around 25% of patients suffer from post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) after cardiac surgery, which often results in persistent pain. This study aims to investigate risk factors for persistent pain in order to adapt current therapy protocols.
conditions: PICS (post-intensive care syndrome) is a symptom complex that can occur after just 24 hours in an intensive care unit and persists for several years.

interventions.name: Perioperative evaluation of cardiac surgery patients

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Cardiac surgery
- Intensive care treatment 
- In domo ≥3 days
- Signed declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients unable to give consent 
- Diagnosis of dementia, cognitive impairment, CNS damage
- Endocarditis
